scope: Test whether one public NIST AMMT X16 layer can be converted from an aggregate statement about dropped frames into an identity-indexed trigger-to-frame ledger, then repeat the frozen adjudication on one untouched layer.
inputsInspectedBeforeSeal: NIST NERDm record mds2-2309 version 1.1.1, including component names, byte sizes, archive SHA-256 values, issue history, and download URLs.
NIST Overhang X16 User Notes pages 3-4, including the stated file naming convention, trigger/frame paragraph, and archive grouping.
HTTP HEAD metadata for the first XYPT, MPM AVI, and MPM TIFF archives.
A response-headers-only range probe against the final 65,536 bytes of XYPT_L001-025.zip; the 206 body was not consumed or stored.
notInspectedBeforeSeal: ZIP central-directory entries or local-file headers from any X16 data archive.
Any XYPT command row, AVI header, frame index, TIFF IFD, pixel value, or layer-specific count.
Any result-derived choice of development or holdout layer.

fixedLayerRoles.rule: Use L0001 to develop parsers and adjudication. Do not inspect L0002 member bytes or layer-specific counts until the L0001 result, parser version, and any amendments are committed and pushed. No substitution is allowed because a layer is inconvenient or contradicts a hypothesis.

claimsUnderTest.claim: The User Notes sentence is literally correct: the number of nonzero XYPT triggers is lower than the number of associated MPM frames.
claimsUnderTest.prediction: frameCount - triggerCount is positive on L0001 and repeats in sign on L0002.
claimsUnderTest.reject: frameCount is less than or equal to triggerCount on either adjudicated layer.

claimsUnderTest.claim: The intended dropped-frame model is correct: MPM has no more frames than nonzero XYPT triggers, the deficit is at most 20, and every absent frame is at the end.
claimsUnderTest.prediction: 0 <= triggerCount - frameCount <= 20 and public bytes independently locate the deficit after the final present trigger.
claimsUnderTest.reject: The deficit is negative or exceeds 20, or the bytes cannot distinguish an end-only loss from an internal loss with the same count.

claimsUnderTest.claim: The public XYPT and MPM members contain enough identity information to reconstruct authenticated null slots rather than only a count deficit.
claimsUnderTest.prediction: Every decoded frame carries a trigger identifier, timestamp, monotone acquisition counter, or another documented key that maps it to exactly one expected nonzero-trigger slot.
claimsUnderTest.reject: Frames expose only ordinal order or aggregate count, so two different missing-slot placements yield identical public observations.

claimsUnderTest.claim: HTTP range access can adjudicate the layer without downloading either multi-gigabyte MPM archive.
claimsUnderTest.prediction: ZIP64 directories, the complete L0001 XYPT member, and sufficient AVI/TIFF header or index bytes are retrieved in at most 134217728 transferred bytes per layer.
claimsUnderTest.reject: A required member is deflated or indexed so that adjudication exceeds the fixed byte budget.

claimsUnderTest.claim: The frozen L0001 procedure transfers without modification to untouched L0002.
claimsUnderTest.prediction: Two independent implementations reproduce both layer counts, range receipts, member hashes where complete extraction occurs, and the same qualification verdict.
claimsUnderTest.reject: Any parser, count rule, missingness rule, or byte budget must change after viewing L0002.

adjudicationChain: Official archive size and SHA-256 plus fixed layer role
ZIP/ZIP64 central directory and local-header agreement
Complete XYPT member with stable member hash and documented trigger rule
MPM container header/index with independently reproduced frame count
Presence or absence of a per-frame slot key
Count deficit and all slot placements compatible with the public bytes
Exact null ledger only if every compatible placement is a singleton

fixedCountingRules.triggerCount: Parse the complete XYPT text. Identify the trigger field from the documented header or X4 primary format; count rows whose trigger value is nonzero. Preserve the total row count and a SHA-256 of the extracted member.
fixedCountingRules.frameCount: Prefer container-native counts that can be cross-checked: AVI main header total frames, stream header length, OpenDML total frames, movi chunk/index count, or TIFF IFD count. Report every available count; disagreement is inconclusive and may not be resolved by choosing the preferred value.
fixedCountingRules.slotIdentity: An ordinal frame number is not a trigger identity. A slot is located only by a documented trigger ID, acquisition counter, timestamp with a one-to-one tolerance rule fixed on L0001, or a public integrity record that independently proves tail-only truncation.
fixedCountingRules.nullLedger: Return exact only when the set of missing-slot placements compatible with all public bytes has cardinality one; otherwise return set-valued or not-identifiable.

transferBudget.countsTowardBudget: All response bodies from XYPT and MPM ZIP range requests, including repeated ranges and failed overfetches.
transferBudget.doesNotCount: The 80 kB NERDm JSON, 391 kB User Notes PDF, and response headers obtained before sealing.
transferBudget.stop: Stop archive acquisition for the layer before the next request would exceed the budget. Do not fall back to a whole-archive download.

independenceAndHoldout.implementationA: Node.js range/ZIP/container parser developed only on L0001.
independenceAndHoldout.implementationB: Python parser that independently implements range receipts and count extraction without importing implementation A outputs.
independenceAndHoldout.holdoutSeal: L0002 is not requested until implementation A, the L0001 result, and all amendments are committed and pushed.
forbidden: Changing the trigger definition after seeing which count is closer to the frame count.
Assuming missing frames lie at the end solely because the User Notes say they are primarily missing there.
Treating a ZIP member ordinal, AVI frame ordinal, or TIFF IFD ordinal as an authenticated XYPT slot key.
Using L0002 to repair a parser without recording and sealing an amendment before reinspection.

successCriteria: Both archive central directories and selected local headers agree on name, method, compressed size, uncompressed size, CRC-32, and offset.
The complete L0001 XYPT member is extracted and hash-bound within the transfer budget.
At least two independent container counters agree on the L0001 MPM frame count, or the result is explicitly inconclusive.
The possible missing-slot set is computed rather than replaced by an end-loss assumption.
Independent implementations agree on every recorded count and qualification verdict.
The frozen procedure is applied unchanged to L0002 after the development result is sealed.
stopRules: Stop with not-identifiable if public MPM bytes lack a per-frame slot key and more than one missing-slot placement is compatible.
Stop with inconclusive if native frame counters disagree and the fixed byte budget cannot resolve them.
Stop with access-boundary if NIST range responses cease to be byte-stable or ignore requested ranges.
Stop before holdout if any development-result amendment remains unsealed.
Do not claim sensor-domain independence, process-temperature accuracy, or physical-event truth from a trigger-frame ledger.
safetyPrivacyEthics: The cycle reads public machine-process files only, makes no hardware actuation, accesses no personal or restricted records, and limits network transfer by fixed budget.
